learning: Compare against iteration 1. If slalom line_loss_events fall below 2.0 and steering_oscillation on the s-bend stays near or below 0.27, keep the controller. If slalom losses stay at 2.0 with max_error at 0.06 or above, the limit is yaw response, so test the Builder's wheel_track 0.10 m. If oscillation rises above about 0.3 with kd 0.8, reduce kd toward 0.5 before changing kp.
notes: Sensor size 0.016 m with the iteration 1 row, plus a slower base speed (1.1) and more derivative damping (kd 0.8) for the s-bend and slalom overshoot. kp is held at 5.0.
rationale: Iteration 1 is the only race evidence. The widened row (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m) roughly doubled oval progress (0.95 with 70% finishes) and lifted s-bend progress from 0.14 to 0.38. The s-bend and slalom still end off-track. Max_error sits at about 0.064 m, just past the 0.06 m limit, and steering_oscillation is 0.265 on the s-bend, so the controller is overshooting on alternating bends. The slalom loses the line exactly 2.0 times per run. The geometry now changes sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m, which should give more tape signal per sensor and reduce those losses. Because the signal is a weighted average, that change should leave the signal scale roughly the same. I keep the iteration 1 weights and line-loss rule, and make two controller changes. First, base_speed drops from 1.2 to 1.1 to give the steering more time on tight bends. The oval's completion time rises from about 1.9 s to about 2.1 s, which is still inside the 3 s limit. Second, kd rises from 0.6 to 0.8 to damp the overshoot that shows as oscillation. kp stays at 5.0 because iteration 1 showed that a stronger gain was needed to finish the oval. Expected result, unmeasured: fewer slalom line losses from the larger footprint, and less s-bend oscillation from the damping. If max_error still exceeds 0.06 with oscillation at or below 0.27, the limit is yaw response, which the Builder's wheel_track test addresses.
